primitives.name: Central Limit Theorem Strategy Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: - The "CLT Rule": when choosing between strategies, evaluate Z — an underdog (μ < μ_opp) gains by increasing σ2 (more variance), a favorite gains by decreasing it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Z': 'dimensionless Z-score', '\\mu': 'mean score expected per play (points)', '\\mu_{\\text{opp}}': 'opponent mean score (points)', '\\sigma^2': "variance of team's score (points²)", '\\sigma_{\\text{opp}}^2': 'opponent score variance (points²)'}
primitives.assumptions: Normality of score distribution via CLT, fixed opponent parameters, static play values and probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Z approaches zero or exceeds ±3, CLT approximation fails due to non-normality or extreme skewness.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses Z to compute variance tilt factor for 4th-down decisions; GSI computes win probability via erf(Z/√2) from empirical drive data.
layer2.telemetry: Mean win probability added by variance-tilted vs baseline 4th-down recommendations.

primitives.name: Mean-Variance Score Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Total score mean μ = Σ_i v_i N_i p_i and variance σ2 = Σ_i v_i2 N_i p_i(1-p_i).
primitives.latex: \mu = \sum_i v_i N_i p_i, \quad \sigma^2 = \sum_i v_i^2 N_i p_i(1-p_i)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mu': 'expected score (points)', '\\sigma^2': 'score variance (points²)', 'v_i': 'point value of play type i (points)', 'N_i': 'usage count of play type i (dimensionless)', 'p_i': 'success probability of play type i (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Play outcomes modeled as Bernoulli trials, linear additive score contributions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-Bernoulli outcomes or correlated plays invalidate the variance decomposition.

layer2.mapping: GSE maps play usage allocations {N_i} to μ and σ²; GSI evaluates Z from these to infer strategy.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical score variance vs predicted variance from nflverse drive data.

primitives.name: Skill Curve Play Allocation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Skill-curve extension: p_i(N_i) = α_i - β_i N_i/N (success rate declines as a play is overused); optimal mix then interior rather than all-or-nothing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_i(N_i)': 'conditional success probability of play i (dimensionless)', '\\alpha_i': 'base success rate of play i (dimensionless)', '\\beta_i': 'decline rate of play i (dimensionless)', 'N_i': 'usage count of play i (dimensionless)', 'N': 'total number of plays (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Success probability decays linearly with overuse, fixed play set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N_i/N approaches 1, p_i may become negative or exceed unity.

layer2.mapping: GSE adjusts play weights dynamically based on skill curve; GSI uses this to refine Z-score estimates.
layer2.telemetry: Optimal N_3/N ratio from skill curve vs observed usage in nflverse.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that underdogs benefit from increasing variance in their scoring strategy, while favorites should reduce it. This is formalized through the Z-score derived from the Central Limit Theorem, which approximates win probability as a function of mean and variance differences between teams. The mean score μ and its variance σ² are computed from play values, usage counts, and success probabilities. When μ < μ_opp, increasing σ² improves Z and thus win probability. The CLT Rule provides a dual strategy: underdogs seek variance, favorites mitigate it. The skill curve introduces a feedback mechanism where overuse reduces effectiveness, necessitating interior solutions rather than pure exploitation. These primitives form a coherent framework for optimizing play selection in asymmetric games.
